key_insight: A lightweight phone-based, closed-loop interface lets humans provide targeted corrective demonstrations during robot operation so policies can be patched instantly — combining the scalability of handheld data collection with the effectiveness of interactive correction.
problem_solved: Handheld demonstration collection is scalable but open‑loop and misses critical failure states; interactive imitation (e.g., DAgger) fixes covariate shift but is hard to scale physically. RoboPocket enables scalable, in‑the‑wild, corrective feedback that addresses covariate shift and inefficient coverage.
method: Phone app streams robot state and video to a human operator and allows quick corrective inputs (teleoperation labels or action overrides) in real time.
System actively identifies critical states to query or accept retroactive corrections, aggregates corrections into a dataset, and applies lightweight online policy patches for immediate improvement.
Corrective interactions are synchronized with continual offline aggregation for robust retraining, preserving scalability while delivering instant safety/skill fixes on deployment.
impact: Practitioners get a practical way to close the loop on large-scale, in‑the‑wild data collection: faster iteration, fewer catastrophic failures, and better sample efficiency when training robot policies without requiring expensive, co‑located supervision.
